title: Gateway: standardize request_id propagation across streaming + non-streaming errors
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: - All error responses (JSON + streaming SSE) now include a stable `request_id` field. - Gateway now guarantees a request_id is generated and propagated downstream, and echoed back to clients via `x-request-id`.
description:
Context: SDK parity work (ENG-5120) and Support/Oncall feedback (INT-1182) highlighted that `request_id` is not reliably present across all failure modes. Specifically: (1) some gateway-generated errors returned `x-request-id` header but omitted `request_id` in JSON bodies, (2) upstream service errors sometimes used `requestId` or `trace_id` and the gateway passed them through inconsistently, and (3) streaming (SSE) error paths frequently dropped request_id entirely (disconnects, mid-stream 429/5xx, proxy-induced truncations), which made customer triage painful.

This PR standardizes request ID behavior end-to-end: the gateway guarantees a canonical request identifier exists for every request, propagates it to downstream services, and returns it consistently to the caller in both headers and error bodies/events.

What changed (high level):
- Canonicalization: adopt a single canonical field name `request_id` in all JSON error bodies and SSE error payloads.
- Header contract: gateway always sets `x-request-id` on responses (success + error). If a valid request id is already present in inbound `x-request-id`, we honor it; otherwise we generate one.
- Downstream propagation: gateway forwards `x-request-id` to downstream HTTP services and gRPC metadata so services can log it and (optionally) reflect it.
- Error normalization: map upstream variants (`requestId`, `trace_id`, `x-request-id`) into the canonical `request_id` field before returning to clients.
- Streaming: ensure the initial SSE metadata event includes `request_id`, and any SSE error event emitted by the gateway includes `request_id` even when the upstream stream fails mid-flight.

Why this is safe:
- No behavior change to success payload schemas.
- Adds fields/headers only; does not remove existing error fields (we keep legacy fields in internal logs only; client-facing remains canonicalized).
- Request IDs are non-secret; security review confirms they are safe to log and share with Support, and do not encode sensitive information.

Testing:
- Added unit tests for request-id selection/generation and upstream error normalization.
- Added integration tests for: JSON 429 with Retry-After, JSON 500, SSE mid-stream upstream 502, and gateway-generated 401/403 errors.

Follow-ups:
- SDKs will rely on this contract in their typed errors and conformance fixtures (ENG-5126 / ENG-5127).
commits: gateway: introduce request id resolver + canonicalization helpers
gateway: always attach x-request-id to responses (success + error)
gateway: normalize upstream error shapes into request_id
streaming: include request_id in initial meta event + error events
tests: add integration coverage for streaming + non-streaming failures
conversation:
Allison Grant (review): Can we ensure request_id is present on gateway-generated 401/403 as well? Those are the most common support escalations because customers can’t provide anything besides timestamps. Also please confirm we’re not generating a new request id when one is already present in inbound x-request-id; I want a single correlation id across proxies.

Ethan Park (author): Good call. Updated middleware so request_id is resolved before auth and attached to the response headers even for auth failures. Also made inbound x-request-id precedence explicit (we accept if it matches our validator; otherwise we generate). Added tests for 401 and malformed inbound header.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): For downstream propagation, we should forward x-request-id to the auth/policy service too; it’s the one we look at during incident debugging. Also, please align naming: we’ve used x-request-id historically (not x-redwood-request-id). Let’s keep x-request-id as the canonical header.

Ethan Park (author): Agreed — kept x-request-id canonical, removed x-redwood-request-id from earlier draft. Added propagation to auth/policy client and updated docs/internal/api-errors.md accordingly.

Ibrahim Khan (review): Streaming semantics: how do we guarantee request_id when the stream dies before the first chunk? The SDKs need a stable place to read it. If we only emit it in a meta event after the upstream yields, we’ll still miss some cases.

Ethan Park (author): Updated SSE writer to emit an immediate `event: meta` frame containing request_id as soon as headers are committed (before proxying upstream chunks). If the upstream fails before producing tokens, the client still receives meta + error with request_id. Added integration test simulating upstream connection failure before first token.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please consider rate-limit storms: does emitting meta before first byte change buffering/flush behavior? Also, confirm we don’t log request headers containing API keys.

Ethan Park (author): Meta event is a tiny frame (~60–90 bytes) and uses existing flush behavior; it doesn’t increase request fanout. No changes to header logging; request-id middleware only reads x-request-id and does not touch auth headers. Marcus also reviewed secret-handling implications below.

Marcus Lin (security review): Looks fine. Ensure request_id is randomly generated (no user-controlled concatenation), validate inbound request id characters/length to prevent log injection, and keep it out of any user-visible error messages besides the field itself.

Ethan Park (author): Implemented strict validator (UUIDv7 or 20–64 chars base62 with dashes/underscores), otherwise generate UUIDv7. Added test cases for newline/oversize inbound header. Client-visible output is only `request_id` field + x-request-id header.

Allison Grant (approval): Approved after tests. Please sync with observability-pack dashboards so request_id is extracted consistently from error payloads.

Ethan Park (author): Will follow up in observability-pack; for now, logs already include request_id and dashboards can join on it.

Result: Merged via squash. Gateway deploy scheduled with next weekday release window; coordinated with ENG-5130 rollout checklist.
